Grid system

Grid system — spec and stress test

Every dashed box is a stage: drag its bottom-right corner, or use the width buttons above. Each stage reports its width, how many items share the first row, and whether anything overflows. Tests 9 to 13 are size-driven: they also report the container width and which size is active, and fail if the column count is not the one asked for at that size. Hazard marks a failure the design already predicts; Overflow in red is an unexpected one. The CSS under test is the framework's own (css/mycss.css); this page adds no layout rules.

Self-test

Sweeps every stage across 16 widths in five modes (default, compact, spacious, RTL, long content). Copy the box below to report a browser.

0 · Sizes: width tokens, fold points and container sizes

Resolved live from the token CSS: content widths and fold points, not viewport breakpoints. The last six rows are the container sizes; they are measured on the nearest .c-container, never the viewport.

TokenResolves toRoleScale (÷ 4)

1 · Smart grid — baseline

.c-grid

The existing composition, re-expressed with the new maths. Must behave exactly as before: as many 256px-minimum columns as fit.

2 · Column cap

--my-grid-columns: 3

Never more than 3 per row, still wraps to 2 and 1 on its own. Replaces Bulma's fixed-grid column counts without any breakpoint.

2b · Cap of 4 with a smaller minimum

--my-grid-columns: 4; --my-grid-min: var(--my-space-40)

2c · Cap + a gap utility

.c-grid | u-gutter-lg

Was a hazard: u-gutter-* set gap behind the cap's back, giving 2 columns where 3 were asked. The utilities now publish their gap as --my-column-gap, the grid reads it, and you get the 3 you asked for. (A wider gap still means the row wraps a little sooner than test 2; that is correct.)

2d · Flex 8 / 4 + gap utilities

.c-columns | u-gutter-lg and | u-inline-xs

Same check for the flex columns, with a larger and a smaller gap than the default. Both rows must still split 8 / 4 when there is room.

3b · Spans in a smart grid — the unsafe one

grid-column: span 2

Numeric spans are deliberately not offered on the smart grid: once only one column fits, a span of 2 forces an extra track. The other items come up one gap short, and below about 290px the grid overflows.

4 · Fixed grid + cells

.c-container > .c-grid[data-layout="fixed"]

No sized knobs at all: cells set --my-cell-span / --my-cell-start. Default behaviour is one column below md (768px of container), 12 tracks from there up.

4c · Fixed grid with no container

.c-grid[data-layout="fixed"] without .c-container

Nothing to query, so it stays at its xs default of one column at every width. That is the safe failure: stacked, never overflowing. (Setting --my-grid-columns-xs: 12 would force tracks without a container.)

9 · Column count by size

--my-grid-columns-xs: 2; -md: 3; -xl: 6

Exact counts chosen per container size, no spans needed. A sized knob holds from its size up until a larger one takes over, so sm and lg inherit from the size below.

10 · Spans by size

--my-cell-span: 12; -sm: 6; -lg: 4; -xl: 3

12 tracks from sm up (--my-grid-columns-sm: 12); each card is full, then half, a third, a quarter.

10b · Layout that changes shape by size

--my-cell-span-* + --my-cell-start-*

Stacked, then nav 4 + main 8, then nav 3 + main 6 + aside 3. The note cell is offset with a start that only applies from lg; below that the clamp keeps it on the grid.

nav
main
aside
note (start 4 from lg)

11 · Smart grid with a cap that changes by size

.c-grid --my-grid-columns: 2; -lg: 4

Still the wrapping grid (160px minimum here), but the most it may show per row is 2, then 4 from lg. The cap is a ceiling, not a count: it never forces columns narrower than the minimum.

12 · Sizes measure the container, not the page

.c-columns › .c-container › .c-grid

The same grid twice, side by side: 2 columns, 4 from md. Each copy answers to its own column's width, so at stage widths where the page is wide but each half is not, both stay at 2. The readout follows the first copy.

13 · Flex columns with spans by size

.c-columns --my-col-span: 12; -md: 6; -xl: 4

The flex columns take the same sized knob. Full width, halves from md, thirds from xl. The minimum-width wrap still applies underneath, so a span can never squeeze a column below --my-columns-min.

13b · Flex 8 / 4 that only splits from lg

--my-col-span-lg: 8 / --my-col-span-lg: 4

Compare with test 5, where the split point falls out of the minimum width (about 832px). Here it is chosen: stacked until lg.

main
aside

14 · Where a query container must not go

.c-cluster > .c-container

A query container cannot take its width from its own content, so inside anything that shrink-wraps (a cluster, an inline-block, fit-content) it collapses to nothing. It needs a width from outside: a block, a stretched item, a grid cell, a column.

sibling
